- Delta: $58,048M → $61,643M = +6.2% [DOC-1]

**Important comparability caveat:** Alaska's FY2024 figures are **not organically comparable** to prior years because Alaska completed its acquisition of Hawaiian Holdings on September 18, 2024, and Hawaiian's results (post-acquisition) are consolidated into Alaska's FY2024 total. Hawaiian contributed $869 million of revenue (and a $113 million net loss) to Alaska's consolidated results from the acquisition date through year-end [DOC-2]. Stripping out this inorganic contribution, Alaska's standalone FY2024 revenue would be roughly $10,866M, implying 2023→2024 organic growth of only about **4.2%** — below Delta, United, and Southwest, not above them. The other four carriers' figures are on a consistent, comparable calendar-year basis with no noted M&A distortions [DOC-1].

Once the Alaska/Hawaiian acquisition effect is adjusted for, **United Airlines** shows the strongest revenue growth momentum on both a two-year (2022–2024, +26.9%) and one-year (2023–2024, +6.2%, tied with Delta) basis, driven by organic revenue growth rather than acquisition-related consolidation [DOC-1].

ANSWER: United Airlines had the strongest revenue growth momentum (organic, comparable basis) — up ~26.9% from 2022–2024 and ~6.2% from 2023–2024 — while Alaska Air Group's apparent 2023–2024 growth of ~12.6% is not directly comparable due to the September 2024 Hawaiian Holdings acquisition, which added $869M of inorganic revenue.
